title: Skill Sheet: Long Bone and Joint Immobilization
body:
## Before you read the checklist

The national EMT psychomotor exam ended in 2023; these skills are verified **in course** by your program using these same NREMT sheets, and states including NJ accept that verification. Both splinting stations are below because they are graded the same way and share every critical criterion.

> **Key:** Long bone immobilization is `10 points`; joint immobilization is `8 points`. Every line is `1 point` and neither station has a printed time limit. The scored spine of both: check pulse, motor and sensation *before*, immobilize, then check pulse, motor and sensation *after*.

## Station A — Long bone immobilization (`10 points`)

Typical scenario: a closed, angulated or painful, swollen, deformed forearm or lower leg with no life threats.

1. Takes or verbalizes appropriate PPE precautions — `1`
2. Directs application of manual stabilization of the injury — `1`
3. Assesses distal circulation, motor function and sensation in the injured extremity — `1` (`3` findings, one line)

**Evaluator note:** the extremity is warm, pink, with good pulses, movement and sensation.

4. Measures the splint — `1`
5. Applies the splint — `1`
6. Immobilizes the joint above the injury site — `1`
7. Immobilizes the joint below the injury site — `1`
8. Secures the entire injured extremity — `1`
9. Immobilizes the hand or foot in a position of function — `1`
10. Reassesses distal circulation, motor function and sensation after splinting — `1`

**Evaluator note:** the extremity is still warm, pink, and neurovascularly intact.

## Station B — Joint immobilization (`8 points`)

Typical scenario: an isolated shoulder injury, or a dislocated/injured knee or ankle. Splint the joint in the position found unless it is pulseless.

1. Takes or verbalizes appropriate PPE precautions — `1`
2. Directs application of manual stabilization of the injury — `1`
3. Assesses distal circulation, motor function and sensation in the injured extremity — `1`

**Evaluator note:** the extremity is warm, pink, with good pulses, movement and sensation.

4. Selects the proper splinting material — `1`
5. Immobilizes the site of the injury — `1`
6. Immobilizes the bone above the injured joint — `1`
7. Immobilizes the bone below the injured joint — `1`
8. Reassesses distal circulation, motor function and sensation after splinting — `1`

> **Trap:** Long bone: splint the **joints** above and below. Joint injury: splint the **bones** above and below. Same idea, opposite vocabulary, and the sheets are worded exactly that way.

## Numbers and rules worth having ready

| Thing | Rule |
|---|---|
| Neurovascular checks | before and after splinting, every time |
| Position of function, hand | wrist slightly extended, fingers curled around a roll of gauze |
| Position of function, foot | ankle at about `90` degrees |
| Angulated long bone with no distal pulse | one attempt at gentle realignment with traction, then splint |
| Joint injury with no distal pulse | splint as found and transport immediately; realignment is a medical-direction call, varies by protocol |
| Open fracture | cover with a sterile dressing first, do not push bone ends back in |
| Traction splint | midshaft femur only — not for hip, knee, or lower-leg injuries |

## Critical criteria (automatic fail) — both stations

- Failure to take or verbalize appropriate PPE precautions
- Grossly moves the injured extremity (or the injured joint) during the procedure
- Failure to immobilize the joints above and below the injury site (long bone), or the bones above and below the injured joint (joint)
- Failure to immobilize the hand or foot in a position of function (long bone station)
- Failure to assess distal circulation, motor function and sensation **before** and **after** splinting
- Failure to manage the patient as a competent EMT
- Exhibits unacceptable affect with the patient or other personnel
- Uses or orders a dangerous or inappropriate intervention

## How to narrate it out loud

- **Say the three checks by name, twice.** "Pulse present, he can wiggle his fingers, he feels my touch" before, and the identical sentence after. Two lines, two easy points, and skipping either one fails the station.
- **Delegate the hold.** "Partner, take manual stabilization above and below the injury and do not let go until it is fully secured." You are scored on directing it, not on doing it personally.
- **Talk to the patient before you move anything.** "I'm going to support your arm — tell me if the pain changes." Grossly moving the limb is an auto-fail, and warning the patient keeps them from yanking away.
- **Measure against the good limb out loud.** "Sizing the splint against his uninjured arm."
- **Name each joint as you cross it.** "Immobilizing the wrist below and the elbow above, securing the whole forearm, hand in position of function around a gauze roll."
- **Finish with the recheck plus a plan.** "Pulse, motor and sensation unchanged after splinting. Cold pack, elevate, reassess every `15 minutes`."

> **On shift:** In the ED you will re-splint after imaging constantly, and the first thing the nurse or PA asks is whether the fingers are still pink and moving. The exam habit of checking before and after is the real habit.
